feature: Nonlinear complete curve-image certificates with an ordered fitting map
native_reference: Rhino 8.32.26160.13001 public MakeCompatible, Brep.CreateFromLoftRefit, normalized-length batches and Loft commands
observations: The public distance query proposes a rational parameter spline from the target endpoint displacement along its dominant coordinate. Map controls stay in the target domain, with clamped endpoint values fixed to its domain endpoints. Common-sign weights and C0 source knots make this map continuous and onto the full target domain. Backtracking is permitted by this positional image certificate; no topology or parameter-order claim follows from it.

Two identical control rows represent the target curve as a tensor surface without changing its image. The existing exact surface-image certificate proves that surface composed with the rounded parameter map against the full source. Existing affine-reference, rational extraction, outward interval and Bernstein algebra machinery is reused.

G1 fitting additionally proves strict parameter order using the exact Bernstein numerator A'W - AW' of the rational map derivative. Nonnegative coefficients with at least one positive coefficient certify an increasing interval. Existing exact subdivision handles isolated stationary points; a constant interval, negative derivative, unresolved sign, exhausted work or depth declines the ordered proposal. C0 knots join the certified intervals.

An unrestricted fitter trial would have collapsed a retraced degree-five line to one cubic because the complete images coincide. Native instead uses 50 and 34 controls at the two retained tolerances. The public image query remains valid; the committed G1 path requires the ordered proof and keeps these two Native subdivision cases explicitly unsupported. This is a general derivative certificate, not an input-specific exception.

All four formerly rejected curved initial fits already passed the station reserve but failed the old piecewise affine full-image proof. Their incremental batch parameters match Native within 1.1102230246251565e-16; sampling-clock changes were not needed. The nonlinear certificate recovers all four without changing the admission reserve, station rule or tolerance.

All eighteen Native initial cubics in the older twenty-four curved transition records now reproduce complete native values at 1e-9 on both backends; the six results needing additional pieces remain unsupported. Sixty-four new style, command, frame, reversal, gauge, affine-domain and scale records also reproduce complete native values at 1e-9.

The twelve source inspections retain raw/simplified, single/paired fits and numerical clocks. Paired fitting sometimes keeps more controls than a single-input fit of the same source. All measured sources are C1/G1 continuous and have a public G2 break at parameter 0.5. These facts do not establish general adaptive subdivision.

Independent units cover nonlinear rational and backtracking image maps, source jumps that omit target witnesses, endpoint extent, five matching samples hiding an interior bump, subnormal offsets, overflowing coordinate differences, axes/scales/common gauges, invalid inputs, isolated stationary points and constant map intervals. The natural-knot and oversized-knot fallback tests use unclamped inputs to retain coverage after adding the projected proposal.

Inconclusive or exhausted ordered projection falls back to the existing closest-point proposals without increasing their query/interval budgets. The final fit still requires a complete continuous certificate; sampled agreement cannot establish acceptance. Legacy comparisons retain their pre-existing per-test tolerances and explicit pending cases, including the documented 1e-8 subdivision/ellipse reserve and unequal-region joining gaps.
